fullPassage: By internalizing the opinions of others, we become intrinsically motivated. We do things because it feels right, which is why we are suspicious of others who have ulterior motives or who are extrinsically motivated. This is why paying people for their kindness backfires. Take blood donation. We do this without expectation of reward. In his book The Gift Relationship, comparing blood services in the US and the UK, the sociologist Richard Titmuss concluded that paying blood donors (as happens in the US) was not only dangerous, because it incentivized the wrong individuals and created dubious practices and safety concerns, but that if the practice was introduced in the UK, it would remove people's intrinsic motivation to express altruism, and erode the communal efforts that are the bedrock of the National Health Service. To test his claims, Swedish researchers carried out a study where adults were asked to donate blood voluntarily, or received the equivalent of $7 in payment, or could donate this payment to a charity. In line with Titmuss's prediction, blood donations dropped significantly when donors were offered payment, but not if the money could be donated to a charity. This phenomenon, known as 'crowding out', sullies the good intentions derived from helping others because it removes the intrinsic value we get, which is why rewarding people financially for acts that are supposed to be morally motivated is considered nasty. When blood donors and non-blood donors were tested with a charitable game, in which blood donors were told that their selected charity would receive no more and no less than $7, with the difference being made up by the experimenter running the study and thus their additional financial donations made no difference to the final amount received by the charity, blood donors still gave more relative to non-blood donors for the sheer warm glow they experienced.

questions.passage: By internalizing the opinions of others, we become intrinsically motivated. We do things because it feels right, which is why we are suspicious of others who have ulterior motives or who are extrinsically motivated. This is why paying people for their kindness backfires. Take blood donation. We do this without expectation of reward. In his book The Gift Relationship, comparing blood services in the US and the UK, the sociologist Richard Titmuss concluded that paying blood donors (as happens in the US) was not only dangerous, because it incentivized the wrong individuals and created dubious practices and safety concerns, but that if the practice was introduced in the UK, it would remove people's intrinsic motivation to express altruism, and __________ the communal efforts that are the bedrock of the National Health Service. To test his claims, Swedish researchers carried out a study where adults were asked to donate blood voluntarily, or received the equivalent of $7 in payment, or could donate this payment to a charity. In line with Titmuss's prediction, blood donations dropped significantly when donors were offered payment, but not if the money could be donated to a charity. This phenomenon, known as 'crowding out', sullies the good intentions derived from helping others because it removes the intrinsic value we get, which is why rewarding people financially for acts that are supposed to be morally motivated is considered nasty. When blood donors and non-blood donors were tested with a charitable game, in which blood donors were told that their selected charity would receive no more and no less than $7, with the difference being made up by the experimenter running the study and thus their additional financial donations made no difference to the final amount received by the charity, blood donors still gave more relative to non-blood donors for the sheer warm glow they experienced.
questions.stem: 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 금전 보상 관행이 영국에 도입되면 국가의료제도의 기반이 되는 공동체적 노력을 **약화시킬(erode)** 것이라고 Titmuss는 경고했다.

❌ ① strengthen: '강화하다'는 뜻으로 경고의 취지와 정반대된다.

❌ ③ document: '기록하다'는 뜻으로 부정적 결과를 나타내는 문맥과 무관하다.
❌ ④ celebrate: '기념하다'는 뜻으로 경고의 문맥과 모순된다.
det.tip: erode는 '서서히 약화시키다/침식시키다'는 뜻으로, 바위가 물에 깎이듯 서서히 사라지는 이미지를 떠올리면 기억하기 쉽다.

questions.passage: It feels right to help others in need. She felt it was the right thing to do after hearing the story. Turn right at the next intersection to reach the station. He believed he had done the right thing by donating his earnings.
questions.stem: 다음 각 문장에 쓰인 right의 의미가 나머지 셋과 다른 것은?

det.korean: ①②④의 right는 '옳은, 올바른'이라는 의미이고, ③의 right는 '오른쪽으로'라는 방향을 뜻한다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① right(옳은): 도움을 주는 것이 옳다고 느껴진다는 의미.
✅ ② right(옳은): 그녀가 한 일이 옳은 일이었다는 의미.
❌ ③ right(오른쪽): 다음 교차로에서 '오른쪽으로' 돌라는 방향을 의미 — 나머지와 다른 의미.
✅ ④ right(옳은): 수익을 기부함으로써 옳은 일을 했다는 의미.
det.tip: right는 '옳은/올바른', '오른쪽', '권리'의 세 가지 핵심 의미를 갖는 다의어이다. 문맥 속 동반 어구(turn, thing to do)로 의미를 구분하자.

✅ ① altruism: 타인을 위해 사심 없이 행동하는 것을 뜻하는 '이타주의'로 영영풀이와 정확히 일치.
❌ ② negligence: '부주의'라는 뜻으로 정의와 무관하다.

❌ ④ hostility: '적대감'이라는 뜻으로 정의와 무관하다.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 문맥에 맞게 한 단어로 변형하여 영어로 쓰시오.

det.korean: 성인들에게 자발적으로 헌혈하거나, 7달러에 상응하는 돈을 받거나, 혹은 그 돈을 자선단체에 **기부할(donate)** 수 있도록 요청했다.
det.analysis: ✅ donate: 'could' 뒤에는 동사원형이 와야 하므로 그대로 donate를 쓴다. 괄호의 원형을 조동사 could 뒤에 맞게 그대로 사용하는 것이 정답이다.
det.tip: 조동사(could) 뒤에는 반드시 동사원형이 온다는 기본 어형 규칙을 확인하는 문제이다.

questions.passage: In his book The Gift Relationship, comparing blood services in the US and the UK, the sociologist Richard Titmuss concluded that paying blood donors (as happens in the US) was not only dangerous, because it __________ (incentivize) the wrong individuals and created dubious practices and safety concerns, but that if the practice was introduced in the UK, it would remove people's intrinsic motivation to express altruism, and erode the communal efforts that are the bedrock of the National Health Service.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 문맥에 맞게 한 단어로 변형하여 영어로 쓰시오.

det.korean: Titmuss는 헌혈자에게 돈을 지불하는 것이 잘못된 개인에게 동기를 **부여했기(incentivized)** 때문에 위험하다고 결론지었다.
det.analysis: ✅ incentivized: 주절의 시제가 과거(concluded)이고 because 뒤의 내용도 과거 사실을 설명하므로 incentivize를 과거형 incentivized로 바꿔야 한다.
det.tip: because 뒤에 이어지는 내용의 시제는 주절(concluded)의 시제와 일치시켜야 한다 — 과거 동사는 -ed를 붙인다.

det.korean: 기부금이 자선단체가 받는 최종 금액에 아무런 차이를 만들지 않았음에도, 헌혈자들은 비헌혈자보다 **그들이 경험한 순수한 따뜻한 감정 때문에(for the sheer warm glow they experienced)** 더 많이 기부했다.

❌ ③ only when it benefits us financially: 금전적 이익을 전제해 문맥과 반대.
❌ ④ to satisfy legal requirements: 법적 요건은 본문에 언급되지 않음.
det.tip: 이 문장은 바로 다음에 나오는 'paying people for their kindness backfires'의 전제가 되는 문장임을 기억하자.

ch: only when it benefits us financially

questions.passage: By internalizing the opinions of others, we become intrinsically motivated. We do things because it feels right, which is why we are suspicious of others who have ulterior motives or who are extrinsically motivated. This is why paying people for their kindness backfires. Take blood donation. We do this without expectation of reward. In his book The Gift Relationship, comparing blood services in the US and the UK, the sociologist Richard Titmuss concluded that paying blood donors (as happens in the US) was not only dangerous, because it incentivized the wrong individuals and created dubious practices and safety concerns, but that if the practice was introduced in the UK, it would remove people's intrinsic motivation to express altruism, and erode the communal efforts that are the bedrock of the National Health Service. To test his claims, Swedish researchers carried out a study where adults were asked to donate blood voluntarily, or received the equivalent of $7 in payment, or could donate this payment to a charity. In line with Titmuss's prediction, blood donations dropped significantly when donors were offered payment, but not if the money could be donated to a charity. This phenomenon, known as 'crowding out', sullies the good intentions derived from helping others because __________, which is why rewarding people financially for acts that are supposed to be morally motivated is considered nasty. When blood donors and non-blood donors were tested with a charitable game, in which blood donors were told that their selected charity would receive no more and no less than $7, with the difference being made up by the experimenter running the study and thus their additional financial donations made no difference to the final amount received by the charity, blood donors still gave more relative to non-blood donors for the sheer warm glow they experienced.
questions.stem: 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 'crowding out'이라 불리는 이 현상은 선의를 더럽히는데, 이는 **우리가 얻는 내재적 가치를 없애기(it removes the intrinsic value we get)** 때문이며, 그래서 도덕적으로 동기부여되어야 할 행위에 금전적 보상을 하는 것이 고약하다고 여겨진다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① it increases public trust in charities: 신뢰 증가는 crowding out의 부정적 함의와 반대.
❌ ② it guarantees a larger financial reward: 더 큰 금전적 보상 보장은 본문에 없는 내용.
✅ ③ it removes the intrinsic value we get: 뒤이어 '도덕적으로 동기부여되어야 할 행위에 돈을 주는 것이 고약하다'는 결론이 이어지므로, 내재적 가치(심리적 만족)가 사라지기 때문이라는 설명과 정확히 일치.
❌ ④ it simplifies the donation process: 기부 절차 간소화는 crowding out과 무관.
det.tip: crowding out의 핵심 논리: 금전 보상이 '내재적 가치(동기)'를 밀어내어 선의를 오염시킨다는 것.
